name: Zero Trust
mantra: Never trust, always verify—assume breach everywhere.
when_to_apply: Designing network security for cloud workloads
Handling internal east-west traffic between services
Architecting mission-critical systems
Establishing access controls for sensitive resources
Building a security readiness plan
without_it: Lateral movement after a single breach
Over-trusted internal traffic becomes attack vector
Implicit access grants expose sensitive data
Flat networks with no segmentation
Delayed breach detection due to lack of continuous verification
key_tradeoff: Stronger security posture at the cost of increased complexity, latency from continuous verification, and operational overhead.

name: Energy Efficiency
mantra: Use the least energy possible—every watt matters.
when_to_apply: Designing new workloads with sustainability goals
Optimizing CPU and compute resource utilization
Choosing between client-side and server-side rendering
Selecting storage tiers and data access patterns
Setting up CI/CD pipelines and quality gates
without_it: Wasteful over-provisioning of compute resources
Unnecessary energy consumption from idle workloads
Unoptimized network traffic inflating carbon footprint
No baseline to measure or improve energy use
Sustainability goals remain aspirational with no actionable design guidance
key_tradeoff: Minimizing energy consumption may conflict with performance, availability, or development velocity.

name: Reducing Demand
mantra: Use less so you need less—cut waste before adding capacity.
when_to_apply: Costs are climbing due to overprovisioned resources
Traffic spikes threaten service stability
Backend systems are saturated under peak load
You want to optimize before scaling out
without_it: Unnecessary overprovisioning and inflated costs
Cascading failures under unexpected load
Poor response times from saturated backends
Wasted compute on work that could be offloaded or cached
key_tradeoff: Reducing demand adds architectural complexity (caching, queuing, offloading) in exchange for lower resource consumption and cost.

name: Sustainable Workload
mantra: Maximize utilization, minimize environmental footprint.
when_to_apply: Designing new cloud workloads on Azure
Optimizing existing applications for energy efficiency
Evaluating architecture decisions for carbon impact
Right-sizing infrastructure to reduce waste
Setting organizational sustainability targets for IT
without_it: Over-provisioned resources wasting energy and money
Untracked carbon emissions from cloud workloads
Inefficient code consuming unnecessary compute cycles
No accountability for environmental impact of IT decisions
key_tradeoff: Balancing performance and feature richness against reduced resource consumption and carbon emissions.

name: Least Privilege
mantra: Grant only what's needed, only when it's needed, and nothing more.
when_to_apply: Assigning roles and permissions to users or services
Configuring service accounts or managed identities
Designing access policies for sensitive resources
Onboarding or offboarding identities in the organization
Reviewing and auditing existing access rights
without_it: Lateral movement by attackers through over-privileged accounts
Accidental data deletion or modification by authorized users
Blast radius of a compromised identity is unnecessarily large
Compliance violations from excessive standing permissions
Difficulty tracing accountability due to broad shared access
key_tradeoff: Tighter access restrictions increase security but add friction and operational overhead for users requesting elevated permissions.

name: Hardware Efficiency
mantra: Use every piece of hardware to its fullest before reaching for more.
when_to_apply: Rightsizing VMs and compute resources
Evaluating whether to replace or extend existing hardware
Designing software to support older devices
Choosing between dedicated and shared infrastructure
Optimizing storage with compression techniques
without_it: Overprovisioned resources driving unnecessary embodied carbon
Premature hardware retirement and e-waste
Low utilization rates across compute fleet
Excluding users on older devices needlessly
Inflated cloud costs from idle resources
key_tradeoff: Maximizing hardware utilization and longevity versus adopting newer, potentially more energy-efficient hardware.

name: Self-Preservation
mantra: Build every component to survive its neighbors' failures.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed systems with multiple dependencies
Workload components face unpredictable load spikes
Deploying services that must remain available during partial outages
Introducing new components into an existing architecture
without_it: Single component failure cascades across the entire system
Uncontained blast radius takes down unrelated services
Transient faults escalate into full outages
Recovery requires manual intervention across all layers
key_tradeoff: Increased isolation and resilience patterns add architectural complexity and resource cost.

name: Blast Radius
mantra: Contain the damage before it contains you.
when_to_apply: Designing fault isolation boundaries for critical workloads
Deploying updates or changes incrementally
Architecting multitenant systems with shared resources
Evaluating co-location and resource density decisions
without_it: Single failure cascades across the entire system
Security breach compromises all tenants and data
Deployments cause widespread outages
No clear boundaries for incident containment
key_tradeoff: Minimizing blast radius increases resource cost and architectural complexity through isolation and redundancy.

name: Assume Breach
mantra: Design every layer as if the attacker is already inside.
when_to_apply: Designing network segmentation and blast radius controls
Evaluating whether perimeter-only defenses are sufficient
Planning encryption strategies for data at rest and in transit
Conducting threat modeling exercises
Building incident response and disaster recovery plans
without_it: Over-reliance on perimeter defenses leads to catastrophic breaches
Lateral movement goes undetected across flat networks
Data exfiltration occurs unchecked after initial compromise
No containment strategy limits blast radius
Delayed detection due to missing audit trails and monitoring
key_tradeoff: Investing in layered internal defenses increases complexity and cost versus the risk of catastrophic loss from a single point of failure.

name: Maturity Model
mantra: Know where you stand so you can plan where to go.
when_to_apply: Assessing current workload capabilities across pillars
Planning incremental improvement roadmaps
Prioritizing investment across competing architectural concerns
Onboarding teams to Well-Architected practices
Benchmarking progress over time
without_it: Ad-hoc improvements with no clear progression path
Over-investing in advanced capabilities before foundations are solid
Inability to communicate architectural readiness to stakeholders
Blind spots across pillars due to uneven attention
No measurable way to track architectural improvement
key_tradeoff: Structured phasing provides clarity but can slow teams that need to leap ahead in a single pillar to meet urgent demands.

name: Responsible AI
mantra: Build AI that earns trust through fairness, transparency, and safety by design.
when_to_apply: Designing or deploying any AI-powered workload
Implementing agentic AI with autonomous decision-making
Building content generation or moderation systems
Preprocessing data that may contain biases
Offering AI capabilities in SaaS products
without_it: Biased or discriminatory AI outputs harming users
Lack of transparency eroding stakeholder trust
Unsafe content generation causing reputational damage
Regulatory non-compliance and legal exposure
Uncontrolled agentic AI behavior
key_tradeoff: Stronger ethical safeguards and human oversight increase latency and cost while reducing the speed of AI capability deployment.

name: Reliability Design Principles
mantra: Design every workload to survive failure and keep serving its purpose.
when_to_apply: Starting architecture design for a new workload
Reviewing existing systems for reliability gaps
Defining SLAs and recovery objectives
Making tradeoff decisions between cost and uptime
without_it: Cascading failures from unplanned outages
No clear recovery strategy when things break
Misaligned reliability targets with business needs
Reactive firefighting instead of proactive design
key_tradeoff: Higher reliability demands greater complexity and cost, requiring deliberate balance against business value.

name: Defense In Depth
mantra: Layer your defenses so no single breach breaks you.
when_to_apply: Designing network architecture for sensitive workloads
Implementing Zero Trust segmentation strategies
Controlling east-west traffic between internal segments
Hardening multi-tier application environments
Evaluating security vs performance tradeoffs
without_it: Single point of compromise exposes entire network
Lateral movement goes undetected between segments
Over-reliance on perimeter security alone
Internal traffic treated as inherently trusted
Performance optimizations silently erode security controls
key_tradeoff: Adding redundant security layers increases protection but can degrade performance and add operational complexity.

name: Performance Efficiency Pillar
mantra: Make every resource count by relentlessly optimizing workload performance.
when_to_apply: Designing new workloads for cloud deployment
Scaling systems to meet growing demand
Evaluating performance bottlenecks in production
Balancing cost against performance requirements
Establishing performance testing and monitoring practices
without_it: Over-provisioned resources wasting budget
Sluggish user experiences under load
No baseline to detect performance regressions
Reactive firefighting instead of proactive optimization
Inability to scale effectively with demand
key_tradeoff: Pushing for maximum performance efficiency often conflicts with cost optimization and may increase architectural complexity.

name: Shared Responsibility Model
mantra: Know exactly what you own and what your provider owns.
when_to_apply: Migrating workloads to any cloud service
Defining security controls for a new deployment
Evaluating compliance requirements
Onboarding Azure Virtual Desktop or Azure VMware Solution
Incident response planning
without_it: Security gaps where neither party patches or monitors
Duplicate effort on provider-managed components
Compliance failures from unclear accountability
Misconfigured services assumed to be managed by the provider
Delayed incident response due to ownership confusion
key_tradeoff: More managed services reduce your operational burden but also reduce your control and customization options.

name: Four Vs Of Big Data
mantra: Characterize your data by Volume, Velocity, Variety, and Veracity before designing your platform.
when_to_apply: Designing a new big data architecture on Azure
Evaluating data platform technology choices
Assessing high-availability requirements for data workloads
Scaling an existing data pipeline that is underperforming
without_it: Over- or under-provisioned storage and compute
Choosing tools that cannot handle data ingestion speed
Ignoring mixed data formats leading to integration failures
Trusting unreliable data for critical decisions
key_tradeoff: Optimizing for one V (e.g., velocity) often increases cost or complexity for another (e.g., veracity).

name: Design For Recovery
mantra: Assume failure will happen and engineer your way back from it.
when_to_apply: Architecting new workloads with availability requirements
Defining RTO and RPO targets for critical systems
Deploying stateful services that must survive outages
Planning for regional or zonal failures
Introducing changes that could cause cascading failures
without_it: Extended downtime with no clear path to restoration
Data loss from unrecoverable failures
Manual heroics replacing systematic recovery processes
Cascading failures spreading across dependent services
Violated SLAs due to unpredictable recovery times
key_tradeoff: Recovery capabilities add cost and complexity that must be balanced against the business impact of downtime.

name: Least-Privilege Access
mantra: Grant only what's needed, nothing more, never longer than necessary.
when_to_apply: Assigning permissions to users or service accounts
Designing role-based access for new workloads
Reviewing existing access rights during audits
Provisioning temporary access for incident response
Onboarding third-party integrations
without_it: Compromised identity leads to broad lateral movement
Excessive standing permissions accumulate over time
Blast radius of breaches grows unchecked
Compliance violations from over-privileged accounts
Difficulty tracing actions to specific permissions
key_tradeoff: Tighter permissions increase security but add friction and operational complexity in managing granular access.

name: Principle Of Least Privilege
mantra: Grant only the access needed—nothing more, nothing less.
when_to_apply: Assigning permissions to user or service accounts
Designing role-based access for new workloads
Reviewing existing access policies during audits
Onboarding new team members or applications
Configuring access to sensitive data or resources
without_it: Over-privileged accounts become attack vectors
Lateral movement across systems after a breach
Accidental data deletion or modification by users
Compliance violations from excessive access
Difficulty tracing actions to responsible parties
key_tradeoff: Tighter access controls increase security but add friction and operational overhead for users and administrators.

name: Decoupling Components
mantra: Break it apart so each piece can stand on its own.
when_to_apply: Components have different scaling requirements
Teams need to deploy independently
A single failure cascades across the entire system
You need to replace or upgrade parts without full redeployment
without_it: Single point of failure brings down the whole application
Scaling requires scaling everything together wastefully
Deployments become risky big-bang events
Teams block each other on shared codebases
Technology choices are locked across the entire system
key_tradeoff: Independence and resilience come at the cost of increased operational complexity and distributed-system challenges.

name: Culture Of Financial Responsibility
mantra: Make every team member an owner of the cloud bill.
when_to_apply: Standing up a new workload team
Cloud costs are growing without clear accountability
Teams routinely over-provision resources without consequence
Preparing for organizational cost optimization initiatives
without_it: Unchecked resource sprawl and waste
No ownership over cost decisions at the team level
Budget overruns discovered only at month-end
Engineering and finance teams operating in silos
Cost optimization treated as a one-time project rather than habit
key_tradeoff: Investing time in financial awareness and governance versus letting teams move fast without cost guardrails.

name: Sustainable AI Design
mantra: Design AI workloads that minimize energy consumption and carbon footprint from day one.
when_to_apply: Selecting AI model architectures and training strategies
Choosing Azure regions and compute resources for AI workloads
Designing data pipelines for AI training and inference
Operationalizing AI models in production
Evaluating tradeoffs between model performance and environmental impact
without_it: Excessive energy consumption from oversized models and infrastructure
Unnecessary carbon emissions from poorly chosen regions or compute
Wasteful data processing pipelines with redundant operations
No visibility into environmental cost of AI workloads
Misalignment with organizational sustainability goals
key_tradeoff: Balancing AI model performance and capability against energy efficiency and carbon footprint reduction.

name: PACELC Theorem
mantra: Even when the network is fine, you must choose between latency and consistency.
when_to_apply: Designing globally distributed databases
Choosing between strong and eventual consistency for read replicas
Evaluating latency-sensitive architectures with replication
Deciding CQRS read-side consistency guarantees
without_it: Unexpected high latency from demanding strong consistency at scale
Stale reads surprising users when latency was silently prioritized
Architects only planning for partition scenarios and ignoring normal-state tradeoffs
Poor database technology choices misaligned with actual consistency needs
key_tradeoff: In normal operation, lower latency requires relaxing consistency, while strong consistency demands accepting higher latency.

name: Defense-In-Depth
mantra: Layer your defenses so no single failure compromises the system.
when_to_apply: Designing network security boundaries
Implementing controls after threat modeling
Hardening workloads against assume-breach scenarios
Protecting critical assets with multiple independent controls
without_it: Single point of compromise takes down entire system
Lateral movement goes unchecked after perimeter breach
Over-reliance on one security control
Gaps between security layers exploited by attackers
key_tradeoff: Each additional security layer adds complexity and cost versus the incremental protection it provides.

name: Design For Resilience
mantra: Build systems that bend but never break.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed workloads with multiple failure points
Defining SLAs and availability targets for critical services
Architecting systems that depend on external or shared resources
Planning for partial outages or degraded operating conditions
without_it: Total outage from a single component failure
Cascading failures across dependent services
Users experience hard errors instead of reduced functionality
No recovery path when faults inevitably occur
key_tradeoff: Increased architectural complexity and cost versus the ability to maintain operations during failures.

name: Verify Explicitly
mantra: Never trust, always verify every identity, device, and action.
when_to_apply: Authenticating users or services accessing resources
Processing data modification requests
Granting access from new locations or devices
Evaluating cross-network boundary requests
Implementing API or service-to-service communication
without_it: Lateral movement by attackers exploiting implicit trust
Unauthorized data access from compromised credentials
Undetected insider threats operating unchecked
Privilege escalation through unverified assumptions
Compliance violations from insufficient access controls
key_tradeoff: Stronger explicit verification increases security but adds latency and friction to user and system interactions.

name: Microsoft Zero Trust Model
mantra: Never trust, always verify — treat every request as if it originates from a hostile network.
when_to_apply: Designing authentication and authorization for any workload
Evaluating network segmentation and access controls
Onboarding new services or third-party integrations
Responding to a security incident or breach
Reviewing existing architecture for security posture gaps
without_it: Implicit trust allows lateral movement after a single compromise
Over-privileged identities expand the blast radius of breaches
Unverified requests bypass critical security controls
Security becomes perimeter-only, ignoring insider threats
Lack of segmentation turns one vulnerability into full compromise
key_tradeoff: Stronger security verification at every layer increases operational complexity and can add latency to user and service interactions.

name: Cost-Efficiency Mindset
mantra: Spend only on what earns its keep.
when_to_apply: Starting a new cloud workload design
Reviewing monthly Azure spend reports
Choosing between service tiers or SKUs
Provisioning SDLC and non-production environments
Evaluating feature ROI before implementation
without_it: Uncontrolled cloud spend with no accountability
Over-provisioned resources sitting idle
No baseline to measure cost improvements against
Non-production environments running at production scale
Investments that deliver minimal business value
key_tradeoff: Minimizing cost while ensuring sufficient investment to meet performance, reliability, and security requirements.

name: Design For Rate Optimization
mantra: Pay less for what you already use by optimizing every rate lever available.
when_to_apply: Reviewing cloud bills for savings opportunities
Choosing between consumption-based and fixed-price models
Committing to reserved instances or savings plans
Leveraging existing licenses through hybrid use benefits
Negotiating enterprise agreements
without_it: Overpaying for resources at on-demand rates
Missing reservation and commitment discounts
Unused hybrid use benefits leaving money on the table
Mismatched pricing models for workload patterns
Cost creep with no structured rate review process
key_tradeoff: Commitment-based discounts lower rates but reduce flexibility to scale down or change services.

name: Test Pyramid
mantra: Build a broad base of fast unit tests and narrow the slow, expensive tests to the top.
when_to_apply: Designing a test automation strategy for a new service
Test suites are slow and flaky, needing restructuring
Balancing test coverage against CI/CD pipeline speed
Onboarding teams to sustainable testing practices
without_it: Over-reliance on slow end-to-end tests creating bottlenecks
Gaps in coverage where integration issues slip through
High maintenance costs from brittle UI-heavy test suites
False confidence from too few or poorly distributed tests
Slow feedback loops delaying developer productivity
key_tradeoff: More unit tests maximize speed and coverage but can miss integration flaws, while more end-to-end tests catch real-world issues but are slow and expensive to maintain.

name: Carbon Awareness
mantra: Run your workloads when and where the grid is greenest.
when_to_apply: Scheduling batch jobs that have flexible execution windows
Designing applications with deferrable or shiftable workloads
Choosing regions for workload placement across multiple datacenters
Building sustainability metrics into operational dashboards
without_it: Workloads run during peak carbon-intensity periods unnecessarily
No alignment between energy consumption and renewable availability
Sustainability goals remain abstract with no actionable scheduling strategy
Missed opportunities to reduce operational carbon footprint at zero cost
key_tradeoff: Optimizing for lower carbon intensity may conflict with latency requirements and immediate processing demands.

name: RE:01 - Simplicity and Efficiency in Workload Design
mantra: Keep it simple—every unnecessary component is a future failure point.
when_to_apply: Starting a new workload architecture design
Reviewing existing systems for reliability improvements
Evaluating whether to add new components or dependencies
Refactoring overly complex solutions
without_it: Cascading failures from unnecessary interdependencies
Increased mean time to recovery due to opaque complexity
Higher operational burden and toil
More surface area for bugs and misconfigurations
key_tradeoff: Simplicity may limit feature richness or flexibility, but complexity directly erodes reliability.

name: Cost-Management Discipline
mantra: Make every dollar visible, owned, and intentional.
when_to_apply: Starting a new cloud project with shared budgets
Cloud spending is growing without clear ownership
Teams lack visibility into their resource costs
Preparing for financial reviews or audits
Establishing governance for multi-team environments
without_it: Uncontrolled cloud spend surprises
No accountability for overprovisioned resources
Budget overruns discovered too late
Teams unaware of cost impact of their decisions
Inability to forecast or plan capacity spending
key_tradeoff: Investing in cost tracking culture and tooling versus moving fast without financial guardrails.

name: Design For Usage Optimization
mantra: Squeeze maximum value from every resource you provision.
when_to_apply: Workload has variable or unpredictable demand patterns
Cloud costs are growing faster than business value
Resources are consistently underutilized
Planning commitment-based purchasing decisions
without_it: Chronic overprovisioning and wasted spend
Underutilized resources sitting idle
Missed discount opportunities from lack of usage awareness
Inability to meet nonfunctional requirements efficiently
key_tradeoff: Maximizing utilization increases complexity and risk of insufficient capacity during demand spikes.

name: Just In Time
mantra: Grant privileges only at the moment they are needed, never before.
when_to_apply: Administering critical impact accounts that require elevated privileges
Accessing production environments for troubleshooting
Performing sensitive operations on infrastructure resources
Granting temporary access to security groups for time-bound tasks
without_it: Standing privileges become targets for credential theft
Lateral movement by attackers through always-on admin accounts
Excessive permissions accumulate over time (privilege creep)
Audit trails lack clarity on why access was granted
Blast radius of compromised accounts is unnecessarily large
key_tradeoff: Reduced attack surface versus increased operational friction and access request latency.

name: Architecture Strategies For Consolidation
mantra: Combine resources and responsibilities to eliminate waste and reduce cost.
when_to_apply: Multiple workloads share similar infrastructure needs
Underutilized resources are driving up costs
Teams maintain redundant services across environments
Scaling efficiency plateaus with current resource layout
without_it: Resource sprawl with low utilization rates
Redundant infrastructure inflating operational costs
Fragmented ownership leading to inefficient management
Missed economies of scale opportunities
key_tradeoff: Consolidation reduces cost but increases blast radius and coupling between workloads.

name: Consolidation
mantra: Pack workloads together deliberately to maximize every dollar spent.
when_to_apply: Multiple underutilized resources are running independently
Cloud bills are growing faster than workload demand
Teams manage redundant infrastructure for similar services
You need to simplify operational overhead across environments
without_it: Sprawling underutilized resources drain budget
Operational complexity multiplies with each isolated component
Inconsistent configurations across duplicate infrastructure
Missed economies of scale in licensing and management
key_tradeoff: Higher resource density cuts costs but increases the risk of noisy neighbor issues and broader blast radius during failures.

name: Transparency
mantra: Show your work so users never have to guess.
when_to_apply: Building AI systems that generate natural language responses
Implementing retrieval-augmented generation pipelines
Deploying autonomous agentic AI workflows
Designing user-facing AI chat or decision-support tools
without_it: Users blindly trust incorrect AI outputs
No auditability of agent decisions or actions
Inability to diagnose hallucinations or data quality issues
Erosion of user trust over time
Regulatory and compliance failures
key_tradeoff: More transparency increases user trust and debuggability but adds complexity and may expose proprietary system internals.

name: CAP Theorem
mantra: Pick two: consistency, availability, or partition tolerance—you cannot have all three.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed databases or data stores
Choosing between strong and eventual consistency
Architecting multi-region replicated systems
Evaluating trade-offs during network partition scenarios
without_it: Assuming a distributed system can be perfectly consistent and always available
Unexpected data staleness or conflicts under network partitions
Over-engineering for consistency at the cost of availability
Poor SLA decisions due to misunderstood replication trade-offs
key_tradeoff: Consistency versus availability when network partitions are unavoidable.

name: Design Principles
mantra: Ground every architecture decision in principled alignment with Well-Architected pillars.
when_to_apply: Starting a new workload design
Evaluating tradeoffs between pillars
Onboarding teams to a design methodology
Reviewing architecture for mission-critical or SaaS scenarios
Aligning HPC or specialized workloads with framework guidance
without_it: Ad-hoc decisions with no consistent rationale
Pillar priorities ignored or misbalanced
Design methodology disconnected from quality attributes
Inconsistent architectural standards across teams
Reactive fixes instead of proactive design
key_tradeoff: Strict adherence to principles adds upfront rigor but may slow initial delivery velocity.

name: Criticality
mantra: Know what matters most before you engineer for resilience.
when_to_apply: Classifying workload flows by business importance
Setting SLAs and reliability targets per component
Allocating budget across reliability investments
Designing fault isolation boundaries
Prioritizing incident response efforts
without_it: Over-engineering low-value components wastes budget
Under-engineering critical paths causes outages
Incident teams lack triage priority guidance
Uniform reliability targets misallocate resources
Fault isolation boundaries drawn arbitrarily
key_tradeoff: Higher criticality demands greater reliability investment, increasing cost and complexity for components that may not all warrant it.

name: Design For Operations
mantra: Anticipate failure before your users do.
when_to_apply: Architecting new services or features
Building CI/CD pipelines with pre-production validation
Defining observability and alerting strategies
Planning chaos engineering or fault injection tests
without_it: Failures surface first in production through customer complaints
Lack of telemetry makes incidents opaque and slow to resolve
Repeated incidents with no clear root cause
Operational concerns bolted on as afterthoughts
key_tradeoff: Investing in upfront operational instrumentation and testing increases development effort but dramatically reduces mean time to detect and recover.

name: Observable Systems
mantra: If you can't see it, you can't fix it.
when_to_apply: Designing distributed systems that need end-to-end visibility
Troubleshooting production incidents across multiple services
Building health dashboards for stakeholder communication
Establishing SLIs and SLOs for reliability tracking
without_it: Blind spots in production lead to prolonged outages
Teams resort to guesswork during incident response
Correlated failures go undetected until customer impact
No data-driven basis for capacity planning or optimization
key_tradeoff: Richer telemetry improves diagnosis but increases cost, complexity, and potential performance overhead.

name: Simplicity
mantra: Reduce the surface area so there is less to break and less to misunderstand.
when_to_apply: Designing a new service or component architecture
Reviewing existing systems for operational overhead
Choosing between multiple implementation approaches
Onboarding new team members who must understand the system
Investigating recurring misconfigurations or outages
without_it: Sprawling architectures with redundant or unused components
Frequent misconfigurations due to excessive complexity
Longer incident resolution times from unclear dependencies
Higher operational costs from managing unnecessary surface area
Difficulty enforcing consistent standards across teams
key_tradeoff: Simplicity may limit flexibility and feature richness, requiring deliberate trade-offs against evolving requirements.

name: CIA Triad
mantra: Protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability in every decision you make.
when_to_apply: Designing access controls for sensitive data
Evaluating threats during security reviews
Planning disaster recovery and redundancy
Assessing impact of a security incident
Defining security requirements for a new workload
without_it: Data breaches from neglected confidentiality controls
Corrupted or tampered data due to missing integrity checks
Service outages from ignored availability planning
Unbalanced security investments favoring one pillar over others
Inability to reason about attack impact systematically
key_tradeoff: Strengthening one assurance (e.g., confidentiality via encryption) can introduce latency or complexity that challenges availability or operational simplicity.

name: Shift Left
mantra: Find and fix problems before they become expensive.
when_to_apply: Designing CI/CD pipelines for new services
Establishing quality assurance processes
Setting up observability and monitoring strategies
Planning deployment validation gates
without_it: Defects discovered in production cause costly outages
Security vulnerabilities slip through to deployed workloads
Feedback loops are slow and expensive to act on
Teams spend more time firefighting than building
key_tradeoff: Investing more upfront in early testing and automation versus shipping faster with less initial validation.

name: Stateless Design
mantra: Store nothing locally—let any instance handle any request.
when_to_apply: Designing services that need to scale horizontally
Building cloud-native microservices
Eliminating single-instance bottlenecks
Preparing for load-balanced traffic distribution
without_it: Sticky sessions create uneven load and single points of failure
Scaling out fails because new instances lack session context
Instance failures cause user session loss
Deployments require complex session draining strategies
key_tradeoff: Simplicity of local state access is traded for the latency and complexity of external state stores.

name: Identity-Based Access Control
mantra: Prove who you are, not what you know.
when_to_apply: Connecting services to Azure resources like databases or storage
Replacing connection strings and API keys in application code
Setting up service-to-service authentication
Onboarding new workloads that need access to shared resources
without_it: Secrets sprawl across config files and repositories
Credential rotation becomes a manual, error-prone burden
Leaked keys lead to unauthorized access and breaches
Audit trails lack clear attribution to specific identities
key_tradeoff: Reduced secret management overhead versus dependency on identity provider availability and correct role assignments.

name: Deny-By-Default
mantra: Block everything, then justify every exception.
when_to_apply: Designing network security groups or firewall rules
Configuring access policies for new workloads
Hardening an existing environment with overly permissive rules
Segmenting networks between trust boundaries
without_it: Lateral movement across network segments goes unchecked
Unknown or forgotten open ports become attack vectors
Compliance violations from overly permissive access
Blast radius of a breach expands uncontrollably
key_tradeoff: Stronger security posture at the cost of slower onboarding and higher operational overhead for managing allowlist exceptions.

name: Security Maturity Model
mantra: Progress your security posture deliberately through defined maturity levels.
when_to_apply: Assessing current security posture of a workload
Planning security improvement roadmaps
Benchmarking security practices across teams
Prioritizing security investments with limited resources
without_it: Ad-hoc security improvements with no clear progression
Over-investing in advanced controls while missing fundamentals
Inability to measure security posture improvement over time
No shared language for communicating security readiness
key_tradeoff: Advancing maturity levels requires increasing investment and organizational discipline versus the diminishing marginal risk reduction at higher levels.

name: Least-Privilege
mantra: Grant only what's needed, nothing more.
when_to_apply: Configuring service account permissions for build and deployment pipelines
Assigning user roles within teams or functions
Granting access to production environments
Designing API authorization scopes
without_it: Lateral movement by attackers through over-permissioned accounts
Accidental deletion or modification of critical resources
Compliance violations from excessive access
Blast radius expansion when credentials are compromised
key_tradeoff: Tighter access improves security but increases operational friction and access-request overhead.

name: Infrastructure To Scale
mantra: Build every layer to stretch before it breaks.
when_to_apply: Traffic patterns are unpredictable or spiky
You are designing a new service expected to grow
Current resources are regularly hitting capacity limits
Migrating from monolith to distributed architecture
without_it: Outages under unexpected load spikes
Costly over-provisioning to compensate for rigid architecture
Singletons become bottlenecks that block horizontal scaling
Cascading failures when one component saturates
key_tradeoff: Scalability increases architectural complexity and cost versus the risk of capacity ceilings and downtime.

name: Consolidate Responsibilities
mantra: Stop owning what others can run better and cheaper.
when_to_apply: Team is stretched thin managing undifferentiated infrastructure
Multiple teams duplicate the same operational capabilities
Costs are rising without proportional value delivery
Shared services or platform teams exist in the organization
Managed service alternatives are available for current workloads
without_it: Teams reinvent the wheel across the organization
Operational overhead consumes budget meant for innovation
Skill gaps lead to poorly managed components
Inconsistent implementations increase total cost of ownership
Team burnout from excessive breadth of responsibilities
key_tradeoff: Reduced cost and operational burden versus loss of direct control and potential dependency on external teams' priorities.

name: Cost Optimization Maturity Model
mantra: Evolve from counting coins to commanding costs.
when_to_apply: Assessing current cloud cost management capabilities
Building a roadmap for FinOps adoption
Justifying investment in cost optimization tooling
Benchmarking cost practices across teams
without_it: Ad-hoc cost management with no improvement trajectory
No clear accountability for cloud spend
Reactive bill shock instead of proactive optimization
Inability to measure cost governance progress
key_tradeoff: Moving up maturity levels requires investment in people, process, and tooling that must be balanced against the optimization savings gained.
